claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis (c. 310/320–403); heresy-hunter; Jerome's friend.
The Panarion ('medicine chest') written 374–377 against the heresies.
SCOPE: opens at Heresy I cap. V (Adam as prophet).
Epiphanius was bishop of Salamis on Cyprus from about 367 until 402.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis, in Judea, after 310 and died in 403.
Epiphanius was a monastic founder who spent time in Egypt practicing monasticism before founding a monastery at Besanduk.
The Panarion was written in Koine Greek beginning in AD 374 or 375 and issued about three years later, between 374 and 377.
The Panarion was composed at the instance of correspondents who desired a detailed work on heresies after Epiphanius had confined himself to a list of heresies in his earlier work, the Ancoratus.
The title Panarion means 'Medicine Chest' or 'bread basket,' referring to a stock of remedies to offset the poisons of heresy.
The work is divided into three books comprising seven volumes, with the first 20 heresies prior to Jesus Christ and the remaining 60 dealing with Christian doctrine.
The Panarion is an important source of information on Jewish-Christian gospels, including the Gospel of the Ebionites and the Gospel of the Hebrews.
